Uhud's martyrs were buried in pairs, the one knowing more Quran first, in their blood, unwashed and unprayed for; another report says the Prophet prayed for them.
Jabir moved his father, Uhud's first martyr, to a separate grave after six months, barely changed; the Prophet buried Uhud's martyrs two to a grave, unwashed, in their blood.
Whoever is killed while protecting his property is a martyr.
But for men he cannot mount, the Prophet would join every army unit, and he wishes repeated martyrdom; he announces Zaid, Ja'far and Ibn Rawaha martyred, and Khalid victorious.
Of seventy sent to Bani Amir, all but a lame man are killed after the envoy's stabbing; Gabriel says their Lord is pleased; the Prophet curses the killers forty days.
Anas bin an-Nadr falls at Uhud with over eighty wounds, the verse on such men found with Khuzaima; a convert soon martyred is richly rewarded, and Haritha is in Firdaus.
The Prophet curses Bir Mauna's killers thirty days; some who drank alcohol that morning are martyred at Uhud; angels shade Jabir's slain father; Paradise is under the shades of swords.
Allah smiles at a martyr and his killer, later forgiven and martyred, both entering Paradise; at Khaibar a son of Sa'id says Allah honoured through him a Muslim he killed.
Five are martyrs: those who die of plague, abdominal disease, drowning, or a falling building, and those killed in Allah's cause; plague is martyrdom for every Muslim.
The Prophet would join every army unit but lacks mounts for his followers and dislikes them staying behind; he wishes to be martyred in Allah's Cause, revived and martyred again.
Ten scouts under Asim bin Thabit are surrounded by Bani Lihyan; Asim and six fall, Khubaib, sold in Mecca, prays two rak'at before being killed, and wasps guard Asim's body.
Weeping, the Prophet announces Zaid, Ja'far and Abdullah bin Rawaha martyred before Khalid took the flag unappointed and was given victory; seventy Ansar are betrayed and killed at Bi'r Ma'una.
Ten scouts under Asim bin Thabit are surrounded by Banu Lihyan; Asim falls, Khubaib, sold in Mecca, prays two rak'at before he is killed, and wasps guard Asim's body.
Abdur-Rahman and Khabbab recall Mus'ab's short shroud; promised Paradise, a man drops his dates and fights till martyred; Anas bin an-Nadr's over eighty wounds; verse 33:23 on keeping the covenant.
Asim bin Thabit's scouts are surrounded; Asim falls, Khubaib, sold in Mecca, prays two rak'at before Abu Sirwa' kills him, and wasps guard Asim's body.
Seventy reciters are treacherously killed at Bir Ma'una, including Haram and Amir bin Fuhaira; a later-cancelled verse speaks for them; the Prophet says Qunut against the tribes for a month.
The Prophet would join every battle but for men without mounts who hate staying behind, and would love to be martyred in Allah's cause, revived and martyred again and again.
Of ten men the Prophet sent to scout the enemy, Khubaib was taken outside Mecca's sanctuary to be killed and recited verses on dying as a Muslim for Allah's sake.
The Prophet conveyed his Lord's message that whoever of them is martyred goes to Paradise.
